Hi Daniel — great to connect. Short summary while I pull together the formal docs: 1) BAA: Redwood offers a BAA for enterprise customers. Our standard approach is to execute the BAA for Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments as part of an enterprise contract. For Hosted API customers we can discuss BAA on a case-by-case basis — typically reserved for enterprise agreements with contractual controls and region restrictions. 2) PHI boundaries: Redwood does not persist user input in long-term training datasets. Runtime KV-cache/prefix cache is ephemeral by default; we can configure no-persistence for PHI flows. Audit logs and request/response metadata are retained per tenant policy — default 30 days; retention can be shortened and exported on request.

I’ve attached a clean BAA draft and the initial security questionnaire to start the InfoSec review. Hi Daniel — replying with the concise answers your InfoSec wanted. Happy to expand on any of these during the technical call (I’ve proposed three slots in the calendar link below).

- Hosted API gating: We will consider a BAA for Hosted customers when: (a) the customer signs an enterprise contract with minimum commit levels or usage thresholds; (b) data residency requirements can be met (specific cloud region availability); and (c) the customer accepts the standard Hosted operational controls. For PHI-heavy workloads most customers choose Dedicated or Private for clearer isolation and SLAs.

- Dedicated BYOK/KMS: Yes — Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS keys. You can bring your own keys via our KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and Redwood will encrypt data-at-rest with those keys. Encryption-in-transit is TLS1.2+ by default. Model weights are stored in encrypted object storage and are not exported to third parties; Redwood engineers do not access customer model namespaces without an approved support escalation and recorded access.

- Logs vs. audit trail: Request-level logs contain timestamps, routing/latency metrics, token counts, and request IDs. By default request/response payloads are not retained in long-term logs for PHI-designated tenants — we can configure zero-persistence of request/response bodies and only keep hashed identifiers for traceability. Audit trail retains configuration changes, user actions in the Console, and IAM events for 90 days (configurable).

Next actions I propose: 1) Please return the questionnaire with any priority items flagged. 2) If legal wants to redline, send the BAA draft back; our counsel will review. 3) Book a 30-min tech call (I’m looping Vivek to run this session).
